title: Sweeps and PR review have no proactive failure visibility
description:
From the Phase 4 final review's unattended-failure pass, flagged as a likely-intentional scope gap rather than a defect — so this tick is a decision, not a correction.

CI remediation pages a human when it strikes out. Sweeps and PR review do not: their failures are discoverable only by someone going and looking. For an epic whose whole point is that nobody is watching, 'pull-only discovery' is a choice that should be made on purpose.

The question is not whether every failure deserves a notification — it does not, and an alerting channel that cries wolf is worse than none. It is whether there is ANY path by which a sweep that has been failing every night for a week reaches a human before someone happens to run tk cloud status.

Options the review suggested: a daily digest, or a stale-supervisor sweep that reports runs whose supervisor died. Tick acy landed 'tk cloud supervisor' which answers the liveness question on demand — the gap is that nothing asks it unprompted.

Note this is the same class as Phase 2's hardest lesson, one level up: there, a supervisor could not report its own death; here, a loop can fail repeatedly and nothing reports it either.

acceptance_criteria: Either sweeps and PR review reach a human when they fail repeatedly, or pull-only discovery is documented as deliberate with the reasoning and the command an operator should run.
closed_reason: Completed: a daily digest, so a loop failing every night reaches a person before someone happens to look. Built on what already existed rather than a second mechanism — acy's supervisor query and uls's durable fault record — and it stays silent when there is nothing to say, rather than sending an all-clear people learn to ignore. This is Phase 2's hardest lesson one level up: there a supervisor could not report its own death, here a loop could fail nightly because nothing was asking.
